transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Daniel Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Alicia Torres (Veridian Platform Eng), Rahul Mehta (Veridian Lead ML Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Veridian Security)

Summary:
Quick SDK onboarding walkthrough covering Python + TypeScript packages, environment/auth setup (API key vs OIDC/SAML), Console and Optimize feature highlights, and an outline for a short pilot and benchmark run. Action items captured and next-step scheduling.

Topics:
- install and quickstart (pip/npm)
- REDWOOD_API_KEY and alternative auth (OIDC/SAML)
- local env vs sandbox vs Dedicated/VPC considerations
- console features (cost/latency breakdown, routes)
- Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, caching, quantization)
- pilot runbook and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Daniel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Daniel, AE at Redwood, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Alicia: Hi all, Alicia from Veridian. Thanks for doing this, we've got Rahul and Sofia from infra and security on the line.
[00:16] Rahul: Morning. Quick context, we're evaluating how to add multi-turn product recommender features into our storefront and want low latency but also predictable cost.
[00:27] Priya: Great, that's exactly the sort of workload where SDK quickstarts help. We'll do a live walkthrough of both Python and TypeScript snippets, show how to wire auth, and then hop into the Console Optimize panel to show batching and cache suggestions.
[00:36] Sofia: One ask up front — we need to understand the options for private deployments and KMS integration, plus audit logs.
[00:44] Daniel: Totally, we'll cover high level now and then we'll follow up with the security pack.

[02:05] Priya: Alright jumping in, first the install. For Python we recommend the package redwood-inference. pip install redwood-inference. For TypeScript that's npm install @redwood/inference or yarn add @redwood/inference.
[02:22] Rahul: Is there a version matrix for node/python compatibility? We run Node 18 and Python 3.10 mostly.
[02:29] Priya: Yes Node 16+ recommended, Node 18 is fine. Python 3.8+ for the core SDK. We'll send the exact matrix in the repo readme.

[04:00] Daniel: On auth, simplest is REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var. Example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxx for local work. For production we support OIDC and SAML via the Console for enterprise tenants and you can map roles and RBAC.
[04:20] Sofia: For SAML we need SCIM provisioning and role sync — is that in scope?
[04:27] Priya: SCIM is supported for user provisioning; role sync can be set up through the Console's directory sync. We'll include the SAML/SCIM guide link.

[06:10] Alicia: What about secrets and KMS — can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS or HashiCorp?
[06:18] Priya: Yes, for Dedicated and Private deployments you can bring your own KMS. For Hosted API we encrypt at rest and you can use customer-managed keys for Private. There's a small ops step during onboarding.

[08:05] Rahul: Network — if we want VPC peering or private endpoints for traffic from our app to Redwood, what are the options?
[08:13] Daniel: Three main patterns: 1) Public hosted API with mTLS + IP allow-listing for simple setups; 2) VPC peering/private endpoint for Dedicated customers; 3) Fully Private deployment installed into your VPC/on-prem for air-gapped requirements. We'll map recommended approach for your compliance needs.

[10:30] Priya: Now code sample — Python quickstart. "from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.generate(model='redwood-7b', prompt='recommend products for a user with cart items...')". The SDK also exposes streaming and a simple retry policy.
[10:58] Alicia: Is redwood-7b available in hosted? We're leaning toward a mixed mode, keep some traffic on hosted and burst to Dedicated.
[11:06] Priya: Yes model variants are in the catalog. You can route by policy: low-latency route to dedicated instances, fallback to hosted. Console has routing rules for that.

[12:45] Priya: TS snippet: "import {Redwood} from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}); const res = await client.generate({model:'redwood-7b', input:'...'})". We showed the same pattern but typed. The SDK also has middleware for token counting and logging in node.

[15:00] Rahul: Token counting — we need to estimate peak tokens per second to size pooling. Does SDK expose tokenization hooks?
[15:08] Priya: Yes there's a tokenizer util in both SDKs. For throughput sizing we usually ask for 95th percentile sequence length and expected qps. Optimize can suggest batching windows based on that distribution.

[17:40] Daniel: Quick Console tour — cost/latency dashboards, per-route breakdown, token-level attribution. You can create a route that pins model version, and enable canary rollouts.
[17:58] Alicia: Can we restrict who sees logs in the Console? Role-based access?
[18:05] Daniel: Yep RBAC plus SSO. Audit logs are exportable; we'll attach the audit log docs.

[20:30] Priya: Now Optimize — this is our recommendation engine. You upload sample traffic (anonymized prompts) or link a prompt set, Optimize runs simulations and suggests: batching configs, cache TTLs for prefix/KV cache, quantization profile if good for your workload, and which cheaper variants are within quality tolerances.
[20:58] Rahul: How does the KV cache work with multi-turn state? We're storing chat context on our side, want to avoid re-sending long histories.
[21:07] Priya: The KV cache stores past attention/key-values on the serving nodes; for multi-turn scenarios, the SDK can attach a cache key so the runtime uses prefix KV rather than re-encoding full history. There are limits — we'll send the exact behavior note. Sometimes transcribed as "KV cash" in older docs, but it's KV cache.

[23:50] Sofia: If we use caching, how does that affect PII and retention? We need retention controls and automatic purging.
[24:00] Daniel: Cache TTLs are configurable per route; for enterprise Private you can set retention to zero. For Hosted we have configurable retention and an option to disable caching for sensitive routes. We'll include the compliance matrix.

[26:15] Priya: About batching: Optimize suggests batch windows with the tradeoff curve of latency vs cost. For example, 20ms extra tail latency might reduce token cost by 18% under typical distributions. You can also set hard latency SLOs that block batching.

[28:40] Rahul: Quantization — is it automated? What's impact on accuracy?
[28:48] Priya: We offer recommended quantization profiles per model and workload. Optimize runs a small eval on your prompt set and recommends a profile where quality drop is within a threshold. If not acceptable, we recommend hybrid routing (high-quality model for critical routes, quantized cheaper model for bulk traffic).

[31:00] Alicia: Can you demo the Optimize panel quickly?
[31:07] Priya: (screen share noises) Ok opening Console, here's the project, routes, and Optimize tab. You can upload CSV of prompts, select metrics (f1, BLEU, or custom evals) and Optimize shows suggested configs with expected cost delta and latency impact.
[32:10] Daniel: Note — we include per-token unit economics so finance can see direct cost impact.

[34:20] Rahul: For the pilot, we'll want a small baseline run against our staging traffic. How is traffic replayed?
[34:29] Priya: You can upload replay logs or we can run a proxy that replays a sampling. The pilot runbook will include a safe replay pattern and metrics to collect: p95 latency, cold-starts per minute, token cost per request, and failure rate.

[36:50] Sofia: Security follow-ups — we need SOC2 docs, network diagrams, encryption key rotation policy, and evidence of least privilege.
[36:59] Daniel: Understood. I'll attach the security pack. For KMS integration in Dedicated/Private we'll document key rotation steps. Also note we support envelope encryption if you need an extra layer.

[39:20] Alicia: Are there any gotchas when using serverless frontends with Redwood SDKs? We have lambdas that call the API.
[39:29] Priya: Common pitfall is keeping persistent connections for streaming in short-lived lambdas — for high-throughput it's better to use a lightweight HTTP client with keep-alive in a pooled environment or use a small aggregator service. We'll provide a pattern.

[41:55] Rahul: For cost modeling, can Optimize export the numbers? CFO wants spreadsheets.
[42:03] Daniel: Yes exports are CSV and we can share a sample run sheet. We'll add a template to the quickstart repo.

[44:30] Priya: Quick note on local dev: we provide a sandbox key that hits a small hosted dev environment with limited rate. It mirrors behavior of the real API but with lower quotas. Good for testing integration and streaming.

[46:10] Alicia: Great. For rollout strategy we'd prefer a canary to 5% then 20% with rollback conditions. Is that in Console?
[46:18] Daniel: Yes the route rollout supports canary percentages and automatic rollback based on error or quality regressions tied to your evals.

[48:50] Rahul: Any limitations on model sizes with dedicated pools? We're planning to use a mix of 13B and 70B variants.
[48:58] Priya: Dedicated supports large models depending on instance types; we'll size GPU pools accordingly. For 70B we recommend specific GPU families; I'll follow up with a recommended instance type doc.

[51:20] Sofia: One more question — how do you handle PII redaction in logs?
[51:28] Priya: We offer automated redaction in transit for specific patterns, and redact in logs by default for hosted. For Private, you can configure regex rules or pipeline hooks to scrub before persistent storage.

[53:40] Daniel: Let's recap next steps: We'll share the quickstart repo and Console video, Priya will own pilot runbook and benchmark script, Alicia will share VPC and point of contact, Sofia will enumerate compliance asks.
[53:58] Alicia: Sounds good. Can we tentatively schedule the pilot week for Feb 10?
[54:05] Priya: Yes that works for us — I'll share a Doodle and propose blocks.

[55:20] Rahul: One last nit — competitors. We evaluated OpenAI fine-tuning before but liked Redwood for routing and cost controls. Curious about vendor lock-in risks.
[55:33] Daniel: We support standard model formats for private deployments and try to keep the API consistent so migration is straightforward. Optimize recommendations are transportable as well, though runtime specifics live in Redwood.
[56:10] Sofia: Thanks everyone, look forward to the security docs.
[56:18] Daniel: Thank you — we'll follow up with artifacts within three business days.
[56:25] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution errors present; some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "Redwood Optima" occasionally). We will attach the raw screen recording link in CRM.
